newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 30.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech Medical Chamber is calling on emergency doctors to collect payments for operations equal to the amount they would receive if the value of the points they receive from insurance companies was one crown, which is part of the new list of charges valid from July 1.

- President Vaclav Havel will fly to the Ukraine today for a three-day official visit at the invitation of Ukranian president Leonid Kucma. He will be accompanied by ministers Ivan Pilip, Karel Kuhnl, Jan Ruml and Martin Riman.

- Although the crown is for the time being staying between 18.45 and 18.70 to the mark, nearly half of Czechs are convinced that the current cabinet will not prevent another drop in the currency, according to a survey from Factum.
- Representatives of the city of Prague approved plans to issue bonds in foreign currency worth up to nine billion crowns.
- The Industry and Trade Ministry will send a proposal for its first large intervention in internal trade to help competition on this market.
- In 1996, economic crime cost the state 19.4 billion crowns, which is 62 percent of all losses caused by criminal acts.
- Kaucuk Kralupy nad Vltavou a.s., a leading manufacturer of plastics and elastics, had gross profits of 127.8 billion crowns for the first five months of this year.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - After several inoperative months, Valcovny Trub Chomutov, which was threatened with bankruptcy, began manufacturing again yesterday.

- From tomorrow, Bratislava will refuse to acknowledge its debts to the Czech Republic of 24 billion crowns, which according to Prague, come from the separation of property of former Czechoslovak state banks.
- Last year, Czechs spent more than 4.5 billion crowns on soft drinks. At the top of this is Coca-Cola, followed by Pepsi, then by domestic Toma Cola.
PRAVO - The Civic Democratic Party (ODS) denied on Saturday that it is in favour of premature elections. ODS is prepared to fulfill its election programme until 2000.

- On Friday, Nova Hut Ostrava signed a contract with IFC Kaiser for the construction of a mini-metalworks, which should be finished by 1999, and contracts for a syndicated credit from 17 foreign banks worth $175 million, and a syndicated credit from domestic banks worth $100 million.
- Ceska Rafinerska began manufacturing BA 98 Super Plus petrol, which has a two percent market share, expected to increase.
- Czech Airlines (CSA) had audited losses last year of 207 million crowns. CSA transported about 1.68 million travellers last year, a year-on-year increase of 12 percent.

- From June 28, the EU is allowing imports of live pigs, pork and pork products, semen and pig embryos and meat from black pigs from the Czech Republic, with the exception of nine southern Moravian districts where pestilence was found.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Kaucuk Group and Chemopetrol Group should be delisted today, and their merger should begin with Unipetrol.

- The Bureau for Preserving Economic Competition issued a fine of half a million crowns to Kabel Plus for abusing its dominant position, when it forced its clients to close new contracts for cable distribution.
- During general meetings of Savings Investment Fund (SIF) and 2nd Savings Privatisation and Investment Fund (2.SPIF) on Saturday, it was decided the funds would merge.
- While former Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik is being criticised for taking a managing position in Ceska Pojistovna, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus supports him in this step.
- Social Security will increase tomorrow by approximately 5.5 percent. This will increase state aid for children and other social aid.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
